---
title: "Policy simulator"
subtitle: "Pull the right lever, on Value Added v2.1: what the model says would happen to a school's results, or a whole area's, if absence or intake were different."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
V <- load_va()
I <- readRDS(here::here("data", "inputs.rds"))
# Each school's latest model year: its inputs and its results in that year
lat <- I |> filter(!excluded) |> arrange(URN, desc(year_label)) |> distinct(URN, .keep_all = TRUE)
res <- V$school_years |> inner_join(lat |> select(URN, year_label), by = c("URN", "year_label")) |>
  select(URN, group, obs) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = obs, names_glue = "a_{group}", values_fn = mean)
va <- V$va |> filter(group == "all") |> select(URN, va = va_shrunk)
sc <- V$schools |> select(URN, n = SCHNAME, la = LANAME, rg = gor_name, lad, pupils)
d <- lat |>
  transmute(URN, year = yl(year_label), fsm = PTFSM6CLA1A, abs = PERCTOT, eal = PNUMEAL, ks2 = ks2_c,
            l4 = z_l4, sen = sen_support, ehcp = sen_ehcp, mob = mobile, adm = as.character(ADMPOL_PT),
            age16 = as.integer(age16), gs = as.integer(girls_school), bs = as.integer(boys_school)) |>
  inner_join(sc, by = "URN") |> inner_join(res, by = "URN") |> left_join(va, by = "URN") |>
  mutate(lad = coalesce(lad, la), pupils = coalesce(pupils, 0)) |>
  filter(!is.na(a_all), !is.na(abs), abs > 0, !is.na(fsm), fsm > 0) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
# The fitted coefficients, by group: one named list per group
co <- split(V$coefs, V$coefs$group)
coefs <- lapply(co, function(x) as.list(setNames(round(x$estimate, 6), x$term)))
areas <- list(region = sort(unique(d$rg)), la = sort(unique(d$la)), district = sort(unique(d$lad)))
payload <- list(schools = d, coefs = coefs, areas = areas, labels = as.list(V$spec$labels),
                years = yl(V$spec$years))
# For the prose
b <- function(g, t) V$coefs$estimate[V$coefs$group == g & V$coefs$term == t]
ab_pct <- function(g, rel) 100 * ((1 + rel)^b(g, "log(PERCTOT)") - 1)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## How to use it

1. **Choose a school**, or switch to **every school in an area** to apply the
   same change across a district, authority, region or England.
2. **Move a lever.** Absence is the lever schools and councils can most
   affect. The intake levers ask what the model expects if a school's
   pupils were different, as an admissions change might make them.
3. **Read the result** for every group of pupils at once, the gap between
   disadvantaged and other pupils, and how much each lever contributes.

The address bar keeps your choices, so a link takes someone else to the
same scenario.
:::

```{r payload}
#| output: asis
cat("<script>window.SIM = ", jsonlite::toJSON(payload, dataframe = "rows", na = "null", auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 6),
    ";</script>\n", sep = "")
```

## How it works {#sec-how}

The simulator uses the fitted [Value Added v2.1](method.qmd) models, one for
each group of pupils. Each model explains the log of a school's Attainment 8
by its intake and setting, so every lever changes a school's expected
result by a *percentage*:

$$\text{Attainment 8}_\text{new} = \text{Attainment 8}_\text{latest} \times
\exp\Big(\sum_j \beta_j \, \Delta x_j\Big)$$

where $\Delta x_j$ is the change in each lever (in logs for absence,
disadvantage and EAL, which enter the model as logs) and $\beta_j$ is its
coefficient for that group. Everything else about the school stays as it
was, including what the model cannot explain: its value added. A school
starts from its latest published result (`r tail(payload$years, 1)` for
most), not from its prediction.

For all pupils, cutting a school's absence by a tenth (say from 9% to
8.1%) goes with Attainment 8 `r pts(ab_pct("all", -0.1), 1)`% higher, about
`r pts(ab_pct("all", -0.1) * mean(d$a_all) / 100, 1)` points at the average
school. For disadvantaged pupils it is `r pts(ab_pct("disadvantaged", -0.1), 1)`%, and for
non-disadvantaged pupils `r pts(ab_pct("non_disadvantaged", -0.1), 1)`%.
**The same cut in absence helps disadvantaged pupils more**, so it narrows
the gap.

In area mode, every school in the area gets the same change, and the area's
result is the average of its schools' results weighted by their number of
pupils.

### What it can and cannot tell you

- **It is the model's arithmetic, not a forecast.** The coefficients
  describe how results differ between schools with different absence and
  intake, all else equal. They are not experiments. A school that cut its
  absence would not necessarily gain exactly this, and how it cut it would
  matter.
- **Absence is not a dial.** The absence lever says what better attendance
  would be worth, not how to get it. See [How school absence
  changes](absence_change.qmd) for what moves it.
- **The intake levers are not policies.** They show how much of a school's
  result is its pupils. Moving them is a way of seeing that, or of thinking
  through an admissions change, not something a school can do.
- **The groups are modelled separately.** Each group has its own
  coefficients, so the same change can do more for one group than another.
  The all-pupils result is its own model, not an average of the others.

### What changed from the original simulator

The [original Pull the Right Lever simulator](https://adam-dennett.shinyapps.io/School_Attainment_Policy_Simulator/)
ran on the first model. This version follows [the review's](review.qmd)
recommendations:

- **No Ofsted grade or workforce levers.** They are no longer in the
  expectation.
- **New levers:** SEN support, EHC plans, pupil mobility and neighbourhood
  education.
- **Girls and boys** are modelled as groups alongside disadvantaged and
  other pupils.
- **Area mode:** the same change across every school in an area.
- **It runs in the browser**, with no server.
